$comment: One home per fact, and the names that own it. WHY IT EXISTS: 0.1.415's escape shape is a fix landing in one of several duplicated implementations while the same defect stays live in the others; 0.1.420 extracted the one implementation, and a guard is what keeps "one" true. Extraction without a guard has a half-life here - 0.1.621's README generator re-derived a selection rule that had already been consolidated, and dropped both of its caveats. This file is the register `check_one_home` reads, so consolidating a fact is a JSON entry rather than a new guard. FIELDS: `owner` is the module that holds the implementation; `defs` are definition names it owns - a `def` of one of them anywhere else under scripts/ is the drift, while an import or a call is fine; `patterns` are regexes whose matches outside the owner are the drift, for shapes that are not `def`s, and each carries a `selftest` string it MUST match, because a regex that has quietly stopped matching anything prints exactly what a clean tree prints (FM-24); `retired_defs` are the private spellings the extraction REMOVED - the owner must not define them and nothing else may either, which is how the pre-0.1.420 copies stay gone; `why` is the defect the consolidation paid for. An entry whose owner is missing, or which names a `def` the owner does not define, is a finding rather than a silent skip, for the same reason. A waiver is a written decision: it names the file, the fact and the reason, and an unused waiver is itself a finding, because an exemption that outlived its reason is an exemption nobody decided. NOT HERE: `check_secret_patterns_parity`, whose table is computed at runtime from secret_patterns.MARKERS rather than declared - it is already one home, and an entry could only restate it.

facts.why: 0.1.415 fixed one of several contrast implementations and the same class stayed live in the rest; 0.1.420 extracted this module.

facts.fact: reading custom properties out of a CSS block
facts.why: the same 0.1.415 shape on the other half of the token path: several readers of one stylesheet, each with its own comment handling.

facts.fact: turning markup into the text a reader sees

patterns.note: the shape rather than the range: markup.py spells the range with the characters themselves and a copy is as likely to spell it with escapes, so the guard keys on the lookbehind-space-lookahead shape, which the previous regex - escapes only - could not see.

facts.why: the 2026-08-20 audit found four private strip-tags regexes and two of the CJK-space rule, each a little different, in a tree whose markup.py docstring already listed what that duplication produced.

facts.fact: the version SKILL.md stamps, the release list, and the order two versions sort in

patterns.what: a private reader of SKILL.md's version stamp
a private reader of SKILL.md's version stamp
a private reader of the CHANGELOG's release list

facts.why: every tool read the stamp for itself, with regexes that disagreed on a real document: a SKILL.md carrying another `*_version:` key above the stamp gave the unanchored ones the NEIGHBOUR's value. Three orderings, one of which raised where another returned (). Two `_releases_between` differing by SIGN. And independent scans of the CHANGELOG's headings, one of them into a set, which cannot answer `newest`. The counts are deliberately absent: the first version of this sentence said seven readers and the register found an eighth and a ninth in the same release.

facts.fact: the platform roster and every capability claim on it

patterns.what: a private parse of the platform roster

facts.why: every tool that used the registry parsed it for itself - the driver, the agent evaluation, two generators, the debug log - and not one checked that what came back was a non-empty list. The only careful reader was inside check_repo, which is the wrong direction for a discipline to travel: the GUARD was careful and the tools that DEPEND on the registry were not.
facts.note: `load_agents`, `load_registry` and `_load_platforms` survive as one-line delegations rather than being retired: they are the seams the tests monkeypatch, and a delegation is not a second implementation. What the patterns refuse is opening the file again.

facts.fact: the conformance history rows, and whether they can be trusted
facts.why: every reader of this file answered a damaged one differently: one named which of absent / unreadable / not-a-list had happened, one raised whatever `json` raised, one caught JSONDecodeError but not OSError and never checked the shape, one checked the shape and not the OS, and the path that WRITES caught nothing at all.

facts.fact: what this package knows about a verdict
facts.why: `build_card` parsed the register itself and imported nothing - a fourth answer to the file whose own module comment records `three functions with three different answers to the same broken file` as the reason gate_registry exists.

facts.fact: what an agent can be run as: the vocabulary it offers, how effort reaches it, and whether two model names are the same model

patterns.what: a private read of the recorded vocabularies

facts.why: the knowledge AROUND the three model facts was duplicated even though the facts themselves must stay apart: the driver composed effort into a model id and never consulted the vocabulary, nothing validated a pin before spending a run's budget, the effort tuple was Claude Code's five applied to platforms with four, eight and none, and the recorded vocabulary file was opened by two tools with two spellings.
facts.note: capability, intent and observation are NOT merged here and merging them is the defect 0.1.614, 0.1.623 and 0.1.625 each paid for. One module owns the vocabulary; three callers ask three questions.

facts.fact: what this repository tracks, and every other question put to git

patterns.note: the ARGV LITERAL, not `subprocess.run(["git"` — the first version required the two adjacent, and two callers that built the list into a variable first were invisible to it while the release claimed the consolidation was total.

facts.why: sixteen invocations, three identical `git(*args)` helpers copied into three files, and a `git ls-files` in every guard that needed one, whose FAILURE handling disagreed. Most said `a scan that did not run is not a scan that passed`; two returned an empty list, one of them feeding the English-only red line, so the guard scanned nothing and printed what it prints on a clean tree. Several split on newlines, which is a bug waiting for a filename with a newline in it. A review then found two more the first pattern could not see, because they assembled the argv before calling.

facts.fact: where the repository root is, for a module that was told nothing
facts.why: the consolidation grew five identical private `_root` helpers in the five modules written to end private copies, and the register could not see them because no fact declared the name. One had already diverged, anchoring on its own data file rather than on SKILL.md.
facts.note: the module-level `ROOT` constants are NOT this fact: they are computed before any sibling can be imported, and three of them carry comments explaining their form.

waivers.reason: check_versions is the guard ON the stamp, so it must be able to read a MALFORMED one — `versioning.SKILL_STAMP` requires the closing quote and would report a broken stamp as no stamp at all. The looser regex is stated at the site with this reason.
